title: Topology Matters in RTL Circuit Representation Learning
one_liner: TopoRTL learns RTL circuit representations by modeling register-cone topology explicitly, encoding behavior-aware tokens, and aligning dual modalities under topological constraints.
lead: Register-transfer-level code is not ordinary text. It describes hardware dataflow: how signals move through logic, where state is stored, and how computations feed into one another over clocked updates. A language model that reads RTL as a sequence of discrete code symbols can capture some syntax but misses critical structure, because circuit meaning depends on graph topology as much as on local code symbols. TopoRTL is built around that observation. It decomposes each RTL design into register cones, creates two behavior-aware modalities, injects topology-aware position information, and trains the model to align the modalities while respecting the underlying circuit structure. The goal is a representation that supports power, performance, area prediction and other design tasks because it preserves how the circuit is wired and how it behaves.

problem.h2: RTL meaning depends on topology, not only symbol order
paras: RTL describes digital hardware through signal assignments, registers, combinational logic, and control conditions. Two code fragments with similar symbol sequences can implement very different circuits if their data dependencies are different. Conversely, two circuits may be semantically similar even when written with different local syntax. A sequence-only encoder is therefore a weak fit for the domain.

Downstream tasks such as PPA prediction, retrieval, and generation all depend on structural properties: fan-in, fan-out, register dependency, control-flow interaction, and how logic cones feed state elements. If the representation fails to encode those topological relations, it cannot serve as a reliable basis for automated design tools.

callout.html: Break RTL designs into register cones, represent them through dual behavior-aware modalities, add topology-sensitive positional encodings, and align the modalities with contrastive learning that respects circuit structure.

paras: The paper changes RTL representation learning from text-style sequence modeling into topology-aware multimodal modeling built around register-cone structure.
object.object: the representation space used for RTL circuit learning

hidden.name: topological behavior encoded across register cones
paras: The hidden quantity is the circuit behavior implied by topology: which signals influence a register, how control conditions route data, and how local logic cones differ across designs. This information is only partially visible in symbol order. It emerges from how modules, wires, and state elements connect.

TopoRTL exposes that quantity by making register cones explicit and by encoding positions relative to cone structure and design structure. The dual-modality setup helps because one view can emphasize behavior-related code symbols while the other captures complementary structural context. Contrastive alignment then forces those views to agree on the same circuit semantics.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark the structural behavior information that must survive in the learned feature representation for RTL tasks to work well.

reads.html: The representation must preserve how information moves through the circuit, not merely which tokens appear.
TopoRTL models RTL as register-cone-based dual modalities with topology-aware positional encodings and topology-guided contrastive alignment to preserve behavior information across designs.

mechanism.h2: Why explicit topology improves RTL feature representations
paras: Register cones are a strong inductive choice because they center the representation around state updates, which are fundamental in hardware. Each cone collects the combinational logic that determines the next value of a register, so it naturally captures a functional unit that hardware designers already reason about. By decomposing the design this way, the model starts from objects that correspond to real circuit semantics instead of arbitrary token spans.

Topology-aware positional encodings then tell the weighted-interaction layers where each piece sits in the circuit graph. In ordinary text models, position means symbol index. In RTL, position also needs to express structural roles such as whether two nodes are in the same cone, how far they are in the dependency graph, and how cones relate across the whole design. That extra signal lets the model separate circuits that are textually similar but structurally different.

The contrastive alignment step closes the loop. Because the model receives two views of the same circuit and is trained to align them under topological constraints, it cannot rely on superficial token overlap alone. It must learn a representation that is stable across modalities precisely when the underlying circuit behavior and topology match.

stages.s: align the modalities with topology-guided contrastive learning

math.h2: Align modalities while preserving circuit structure
math.words: The model combines an encoder for topology-enriched RTL inputs with a contrastive objective that pulls matched modality pairs together and separates mismatched pairs, under constraints derived from circuit topology.
symbols: the loss that aligns matched pairs from the two RTL modalities and separates mismatched pairs
the term that enforces structural consistency based on register-cone and design topology
the weight that controls how strongly topological consistency shapes the embedding
two views derived from the same RTL structure that should share the same semantic representation

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose two RTL modules both contain an add operation and a register assignment in text.
In module A, the add result feeds register r1 directly. In module B, the same add result goes through a conditional gate before reaching r1.
A sequence-only encoder may treat the modules as nearly identical because the local tokens overlap heavily.
TopoRTL separates them because the register-cone structure and topology-aware positions differ, so the topology term penalizes collapsing their representations together.
At the same time, the two modalities derived from module A are pulled toward one another by the contrastive term, reinforcing its circuit-specific feature representation.

math.note: The precise topology term may include several positional components, but the key idea is that structural differences contribute directly to the training objective.

charts.title: TopoRTL
charts.note: The representation remains behavior-aware while becoming much more sensitive to the graph structure that hardware tasks depend on.

items.html: If the preprocessing step extracts register cones poorly, the rest of the model is built on the wrong structural units and representation quality will suffer.
Adding multiple topology-aware positional encodings and dual modalities increases preprocessing and model complexity compared with plain sequence encoders.

items.b: Contrastive pairs must reflect real structure.
items.html: If positive and negative pairs are chosen without proper topological constraints, the model may align superficial similarities instead of genuine circuit behavior.

Keep the structural preprocessing faithful to hardware semantics and validate that ablations on the topology terms reduce downstream performance, confirming that the extra structure is doing real work.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Take a small RTL corpus with downstream labels for tasks such as retrieval or PPA prediction. Build one baseline encoder that reads symbol sequences and one topology-aware encoder that uses register-cone decomposition plus topology-aware positions.

The demo should include matched circuits with small textual changes but real topological changes, as well as circuits with varied syntax but similar behavior. A convincing result shows that the topology-aware model improves downstream task performance because its representations stay sensitive to circuit structure instead of relying mainly on text similarity.
demo.closing: The essential claim is that RTL representations become more useful when they are organized around hardware topology instead of only code tokens.
